 Poland Kraków shooting latest updates: six killed and more than a dozen injured, police say
 Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk heads to the city after four women and two men are killed and more than a dozen people injured

Photograph: Omar Marques/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Emergency responders gather after a deadly shooting on November 7, 2026 in the Main Market Square of Krakow, Poland. Photograph: Omar Marques/Getty Images Nadeem Badshah (now) and Hamish Mackay (earlier) Sat 7 Nov 2026 13.22 EST First published on Sat 7 Nov 2026 10.32 EST Share From 2h ago 10.55 EST What we know so far - and what we don't
 Five people have been killed and more than a dozen injured after a shooting in Kraków, Poland
 The gunman aimed at random people as he drove into the city’s main square, a major tourist destination, police said
 The perpetrator was shot and wounded during a confrontation with police
 Police officers are among those injured
 No motive has been announced, but Poland’s PM Donald Tusk says ‘all circumstances’ are being investigated

 2m ago 13.22 EST Two police officers injured in shooting
 An update from Poland’s interior ministry who said two officers were wounded in the shooting, with one seriously injured.
 Share 25m ago 12.59 EST Poland’s PM Donald Tusk wrote on X: “My deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of the victims of the tragic attack in Kraków. The highest praise for the heroic police officers who risked their lives. And a heartfelt appeal to politicians of all stripes: do not exploit this tragedy. We will establish all the circumstances of this crime.”
 Share 42m ago 12.41 EST A man who gave his name as Konrad, and witnessed the shooting, told news website Interia: “I saw shots being fired from the driver’s side window, and smoke was coming out. I ran to the police station in the main market square; when I burst inside, it was full of people hiding on the floor.”
 Share 1h ago 12.25 EST Małopolskie region governor Krzysztof Jan Kleczar told Polsat News that 12 of those injured are in a life-threatening condition.
 Share 1h ago 12.10 EST Death toll increases to six
 The number of people killed in the shooting in Poland has risen to six, the regional Malopolski government said. 
 There are also at least 15 people injured.
 Share Updated at  12.11 EST 1h ago 12.07 EST Poland’s president Karol Nawrocki said his thoughts are with the victims of the shooting in Krakow, which has left five people dead .
 “I am deeply concerned by reports of the tragic events,” Nawrocki wrote on social media.
 He added he remains in contact with authorities and expects “a full explanation of the circumstances”.
 The head of the national security bureau is also on his way to the city.
 “Nawrocki said: “The safety of Poles is an absolute priority.”
 Share 1h ago 11.56 EST The gunman fired shots from a passing car near Slawkowska Street in the main square, according to local reports.
 They were then shot by police officers and detained near the intersection of Dietla and Stradomska streets.
 News website Onet, citing police, said: “The man had no identification documents with him. The police were able to establish his identity through operational work.”
 Share 2h ago 11.43 EST Police: Krakow shooter was Polish national
 Małopolska region police said the perpetrator is Polish, rebuking conspiracy theories on social media.
 They also denied reports that another perpetrator was at large.
 Share Updated at  12.07 EST 2h ago 11.36 EST Courtesy of my colleague Jakub Krupa. Małopolska region police told tvn24 the Krakow attacker, who is injured in hospital, wore “military style” clothing and used “military type firearms”. More weapons have been secured in his car.
 He added the incident has been contained with no other suspects.
 Share 2h ago 11.28 EST View image in fullscreen People stand behind a tape on the Main Market Square in Krakow, Poland. Photograph: Art Service/EPA Share 2h ago 11.27 EST View image in fullscreen Gunshots were fired in the centre of Krakow in the afternoon. An Air Rescue helicopter landed at the scene. Photograph: Art Service/EPA Share 2h ago 11.22 EST The Polish defence minister, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, has also released a statement:
 double quotation mark Tragic shooting in Kraków’s Main Market Square.
 For us, the residents of Kraków and the Małopolska region, these are particularly difficult times.
 I am in contact with the Minister of the Interior, the Voivode and all the emergency services.
 All the circumstances and motives behind this incident will be thoroughly investigated.
 I extend my deepest condolences to the victims’ families and loved ones.
 Share Updated at  11.23 EST 2h ago 11.11 EST Police started to receive reports at around 3 p.m. (1400 GMT) that someone in a car had been shooting randomly people who entered the square, a police spokesperson said.
 “According to information from police officers, the man was wearing military-style attire,” the spokesperson told reporters.
 “During the arrest, officers used their weapons, but the man returned fire; as a result, two police officers are among the injured.”
